item.title: How a GOP redistricting 'dummymander' in North Carolina backfired by 2 seats
item.description: In North Carolina, Republican lawmakers redrew voting maps, aiming to gain one seat in Congress. Instead, they lost two seats, in a classic example of what political scientists call a "dummymander."
item.content:encoded: In North Carolina, Republican lawmakers redrew voting maps, aiming to gain one seat in Congress. Instead, they lost two seats, in a classic example of what political scientists call a "dummymander."
item.dc:creator: Adam Wagner

item.title: The New Yorker's Jason Zengerle on Hakeem Jeffries' rise to first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first-ever African American speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Jason Zengerle of The New Yorker about the rise of Jeffries.
item.content:encoded: Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first-ever African American speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Jason Zengerle of The New Yorker about the rise of Jeffries.

item.title: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history
item.description: President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.

item.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
item.description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

item.title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
